title: Unit – 3 : Session – 11 : SLO – 1  |  Circular Queue — Introduction
sections: A circular queue connects the LAST position back to the front.
Circular queue overcomes the problem of MEMORY WASTAGE (unused spaces) in a linear queue.
In a circular queue, when the rear reaches the end, it wraps around to index 0.
A circular queue follows the FIFO principle.
The condition for a full circular queue is: (rear + 1) % size == FRONT.
The condition for an empty circular queue is: front == -1.
When the first element is inserted, both front and rear point to the SAME (0th) index.
Circular queues are commonly used in ROUND-ROBIN scheduling.
The ISFULL function checks if a circular queue is full.
The ISEMPTY function checks if a circular queue is empty.
Circular queues help in utilizing memory more EFFICIENTLY than linear queues.
In a circular queue, incrementing the rear is done using MODULO (%) operator.
Circular queues can be implemented using arrays or LINKED LISTS.
The front element of a circular queue is accessed using the FRONT pointer.
In circular queues, rear and front move in a CIRCULAR (wrap-around) manner.
